title: Emotions in Depth
subtitle: Nuance your feelings, tell an emotional story, and comfort others

lessons.title: Nuancer un sentiment
lessons.description: Move beyond content and triste to name precise shades of feeling.

blocks.heading: Au-delà de content et triste
blocks.body: At A2 you learned content, triste, and fâché. At B1, precision matters: French speakers reach for a whole palette of shades to say exactly how they feel. Choosing the right word shows real fluency and lets you be understood, not just heard.

examples.french: Je ne suis pas juste content, je suis ravi !
examples.english: I'm not just happy, I'm delighted!

examples.french: Ce n'est pas de la tristesse, c'est plutôt de la mélancolie.
examples.english: It's not sadness, it's more like melancholy.

examples.french: Il n'est pas fâché, il est plutôt agacé.
examples.english: He's not angry, he's more annoyed.

blocks.tip: Reach for "plutôt" (rather) whenever a basic word feels too blunt for what you actually feel.

blocks.heading: La joie en nuances
blocks.body: Positive feelings range from calm contentment to overwhelming joy. Ravi (delighted), comblé (fulfilled), épanoui (flourishing), and soulagé (relieved) each describe a different flavor of happiness.

examples.french: Je suis ravie de te revoir.
examples.english: I'm delighted to see you again.

examples.french: Elle se sent enfin épanouie dans son travail.
examples.english: She finally feels fulfilled in her job.

examples.french: Nous sommes comblés par cette nouvelle.
examples.english: We're overjoyed by this news.

examples.french: Je suis tellement soulagé que tu ailles bien.
examples.english: I'm so relieved that you're doing well.

blocks.heading: La tristesse, la colère et la peur en nuances
blocks.body: Negative emotions also come in degrees. Contrarié is a mild irritation, exaspéré is much stronger. Inquiet is mild worry, angoissé is real anguish. Learning the scale helps you react appropriately.

examples.french: Je suis un peu contrarié, mais ce n'est pas grave.
examples.english: I'm a bit put out, but it's not serious.

examples.french: Il est complètement exaspéré par ce bruit.
examples.english: He's completely exasperated by this noise.

examples.french: Elle est angoissée à l'idée de l'examen.
examples.english: She's anguished at the thought of the exam.

blocks.tip: Native speakers rarely say très fâché — they reach for a stronger word instead, like furieux.

blocks.heading: Le subjonctif après les expressions de sentiment
blocks.body: When a verb or expression of emotion (être content/triste/surpris que, avoir peur que, regretter que) is followed by a different subject, the second verb goes into the subjunctive. The emotion is subjective, so French marks it grammatically.

examples.french: Je suis content que tu viennes.
examples.english: I'm happy that you're coming.

examples.french: Elle est triste que nous partions.
examples.english: She's sad that we're leaving.

examples.french: J'ai peur qu'il soit en retard.
examples.english: I'm afraid he'll be late.

examples.french: Nous sommes surpris que vous sachiez déjà.
examples.english: We're surprised that you already know.

blocks.tip: If the subject doesn't change, skip the subjunctive and use "de" + infinitive instead: "Je suis content de te voir."

blocks.heading: Nuancer avec les adverbes d'intensité
blocks.body: Adverbs let you fine-tune how strong a feeling is, from barely there to overwhelming: un peu → assez → plutôt → très → vraiment → extrêmement → complètement. Place them directly before the adjective.

examples.french: Je suis un peu inquiet.
examples.english: I'm a little worried.

examples.french: Il est assez déçu.
examples.english: He's fairly disappointed.

examples.french: Elle est vraiment ravie.
examples.english: She's really delighted.

examples.french: Nous sommes extrêmement reconnaissants.
examples.english: We're extremely grateful.

examples.french: Je suis complètement épuisé.
examples.english: I'm completely exhausted.

passages.title: Une journée pleine d'émotions
passages.french:
Aujourd'hui, j'ai vécu toutes sortes d'émotions.
Le matin, j'étais plutôt anxieuse avant mon entretien d'embauche.
Mes mains tremblaient un peu dans la salle d'attente.
Pendant l'entretien, je me suis sentie de plus en plus sereine.
Le recruteur semblait satisfait de mes réponses.
À midi, j'ai appris que ma sœur était enceinte : j'étais comblée !
Puis, en rentrant, j'ai vu que mon vélo avait disparu.
J'étais furieuse, puis simplement abattue.
Le soir, mon meilleur ami m'a appelée pour me réconforter.
Grâce à lui, je me suis sentie moins seule et plus reconnaissante.
Avant de dormir, j'ai reçu un message : j'ai le poste !
Ce soir-là, j'étais tellement ravie que j'en ai pleuré de joie.
passages.english:
Today I went through all kinds of emotions.
In the morning, I was rather anxious before my job interview.
My hands were shaking a little in the waiting room.
During the interview, I felt more and more serene.
The recruiter seemed satisfied with my answers.
At noon, I learned my sister was pregnant: I was overjoyed!
Then, on my way home, I saw my bike had disappeared.
I was furious, then simply downcast.
In the evening, my best friend called to comfort me.
Thanks to him, I felt less alone and more grateful.
Before going to sleep, I got a message: I got the job!
That evening, I was so delighted that I cried with joy.

lessons.title: Raconter une émotion forte
lessons.description: Narrate a strong emotional experience using the tenses of storytelling.

blocks.heading: Le corps parle
blocks.body: Strong emotions show up in the body before they show up in words. French has vivid verbs for these physical reactions — useful for telling a gripping story about something that really happened to you.

examples.french: J'ai sursauté quand la porte a claqué.
examples.english: I jumped when the door slammed.

examples.french: Elle a rougi devant tout le monde.
examples.english: She blushed in front of everyone.

examples.french: Mes mains tremblaient.
examples.english: My hands were shaking.

examples.french: J'ai eu des frissons dans le dos.
examples.english: I got shivers down my spine.

blocks.tip: These physical-reaction verbs almost always appear in the passé composé — they describe a single sudden moment.

blocks.heading: Structurer un récit émotionnel
blocks.body: A good story about a strong emotion needs a clear shape: set the scene (imparfait), mark the sudden turning point (soudain, tout à coup + passé composé), then show the aftermath (par la suite, finalement).

examples.french: C'était une soirée tranquille...
examples.english: It was a quiet evening...

examples.french: Soudain, le téléphone a sonné.
examples.english: Suddenly, the phone rang.

examples.french: Sur le coup, je n'ai rien compris.
examples.english: In the moment, I understood nothing.

examples.french: Par la suite, tout s'est éclairci.
examples.english: Afterwards, everything became clear.

blocks.heading: Exprimer l'intensité d'un souvenir
blocks.body: To make a memory feel vivid, French speakers describe the peak of the emotion — the moment they nearly lost control — before describing how they calmed down.

examples.french: J'ai failli craquer devant tout le monde.
examples.english: I nearly broke down in front of everyone.

examples.french: Elle a éclaté en sanglots sans prévenir.
examples.english: She burst into tears without warning.

examples.french: Il a explosé de joie en apprenant la nouvelle.
examples.english: He exploded with joy on hearing the news.

examples.french: Peu à peu, j'ai retrouvé mon calme.
examples.english: Little by little, I found my calm again.

blocks.tip: "Failli" + infinitive means "almost did something" — a great way to add drama: "j'ai failli pleurer" (I almost cried).

blocks.heading: Imparfait et passé composé pour raconter une émotion
blocks.body: Use the imparfait to paint the background feeling or state you were in, and the passé composé for the sudden event that triggered a reaction. The contrast between the two tenses is what makes a story about emotion feel alive.

examples.french: J'étais tranquillement chez moi quand le téléphone a sonné.
examples.english: I was quietly at home when the phone rang.

examples.french: Elle se sentait bien jusqu'à ce qu'elle voie le message.
examples.english: She felt fine until she saw the message.

examples.french: Nous étions inquiets, alors nous avons appelé l'hôpital.
examples.english: We were worried, so we called the hospital.

examples.french: Il faisait beau, et soudain, l'orage a éclaté.
examples.english: The weather was nice, and suddenly, the storm broke.

blocks.tip: State of mind = imparfait (j'étais, je me sentais). Sudden reaction = passé composé (j'ai sursauté, j'ai crié).

blocks.heading: Les connecteurs du récit
blocks.body: Time connectors give your story a clear shape: soudain and tout à coup mark the surprise; sur le coup describes your reaction in that instant; par la suite and peu à peu show what happened afterward; finalement wraps it up.

examples.french: Soudain, j'ai entendu un cri.
examples.english: Suddenly, I heard a scream.

examples.french: Sur le coup, je suis resté figé.
examples.english: In the moment, I stayed frozen.

examples.french: Peu à peu, tout le monde s'est calmé.
examples.english: Little by little, everyone calmed down.

examples.french: Finalement, nous avons pu en rire ensemble.
examples.english: In the end, we were able to laugh about it together.

passages.title: Le jour où j'ai revu mon frère
passages.french:
Ça faisait cinq ans que je n'avais pas vu mon frère.
Ce jour-là, j'attendais à l'aéroport, le cœur qui battait déjà très fort.
J'étais nerveuse, mais aussi impatiente de le retrouver.
Soudain, je l'ai aperçu au milieu de la foule.
Sur le coup, je n'ai pas bougé, comme figée sur place.
Puis, sans réfléchir, j'ai couru vers lui.
Nous nous sommes serrés dans les bras pendant de longues minutes.
J'ai éclaté en sanglots, incapable de prononcer un mot.
Il riait et pleurait en même temps, bouleversé lui aussi.
Les gens autour de nous souriaient devant cette scène.
Par la suite, nous avons parlé pendant des heures dans la voiture.
Peu à peu, les cinq années de silence ont semblé disparaître.
Finalement, ce jour est devenu l'un des plus beaux souvenirs de ma vie.
passages.english:
It had been five years since I'd seen my brother.
That day, I was waiting at the airport, my heart already pounding hard.
I was nervous, but also impatient to see him again.
Suddenly, I spotted him in the middle of the crowd.
In that instant, I didn't move, as if frozen in place.
Then, without thinking, I ran towards him.
We hugged each other for long minutes.
I burst into tears, unable to say a word.
He was laughing and crying at the same time, overwhelmed too.
The people around us smiled at the scene.
Afterwards, we talked for hours in the car.
Little by little, the five years of silence seemed to disappear.
In the end, that day became one of the most beautiful memories of my life.

questions.prompt: How long had it been since the narrator last saw her brother?

questions.tip: She froze for a moment first — "sur le coup, je n'ai pas bougé" — and only then ran to him.

lessons.title: Réconforter
lessons.description: Console a friend, show empathy, and offer gentle advice.

blocks.heading: Trouver les mots justes
blocks.body: When someone is upset, the right words matter more than a long speech. French has short, warm formulas that show you care without minimizing what the other person feels.

examples.french: Je suis désolé pour toi.
examples.english: I'm sorry for you.

examples.french: Ça va aller.
examples.english: It'll be okay.

examples.french: Je suis là pour toi.
examples.english: I'm here for you.

examples.french: Ne t'en fais pas.
examples.english: Don't worry about it.

blocks.tip: Avoid "ce n'est pas grave" (it's no big deal) if the person is truly upset — it can sound dismissive. Prefer "je comprends" (I understand).

blocks.heading: Écouter avant de parler
blocks.body: Comforting someone in French often means listening first. Open questions and reflective phrases (compatir, comprendre, écouter) show empathy before you offer any advice.

examples.french: Raconte-moi ce qui s'est passé.
examples.english: Tell me what happened.

examples.french: Je comprends ce que tu ressens.
examples.english: I understand how you feel.

examples.french: Prends ton temps.
examples.english: Take your time.

examples.french: Tu n'es pas seul dans cette épreuve.
examples.english: You're not alone in this ordeal.

blocks.heading: Des gestes qui réconfortent
blocks.body: Comfort isn't only verbal — a hug, a shoulder to lean on, or simply staying close can say more than words. These expressions describe the gestures that go with kind words.

examples.french: Elle l'a pris dans ses bras.
examples.english: She took him in her arms.

examples.french: Il m'a serré fort contre lui.
examples.english: He held me tight against him.

examples.french: Je suis venue m'asseoir à côté d'elle.
examples.english: I came and sat down next to her.

examples.french: Il lui a offert son épaule.
examples.english: He offered her his shoulder.

blocks.tip: In France, a hug between close friends ("un câlin") is common comfort, but ask before hugging someone you don't know well.

blocks.heading: L'impératif pour rassurer
blocks.body: The imperative is the natural mood for comfort — short, direct, warm commands that reassure without sounding harsh. With tu, drop the -s from -er verbs in the imperative (except before y/en).

examples.french: Ne t'inquiète pas.
examples.english: Don't worry.

examples.french: Prends soin de toi.
examples.english: Take care of yourself.

examples.french: Sois fort, ça va aller.
examples.english: Be strong, it'll be okay.

examples.french: Parle-moi, je t'écoute.
examples.english: Talk to me, I'm listening.

blocks.tip: "Ne t'en fais pas" literally means "don't make yourself [worry] about it" — a fixed reflexive imperative you should learn as a whole phrase.

blocks.heading: Le conditionnel pour conseiller en douceur
blocks.body: To give advice gently instead of ordering someone around, French uses the conditional: tu devrais (you should), il faudrait (it would be necessary), and à ta place, je... (if I were you, I'd...).

examples.french: Tu devrais en parler à quelqu'un.
examples.english: You should talk to someone about it.

examples.french: À ta place, je me reposerais un peu.
examples.english: If I were you, I'd rest a little.

examples.french: Il faudrait que tu prennes du temps pour toi.
examples.english: You should take some time for yourself.

examples.french: Ce serait peut-être bien de dormir un peu.
examples.english: It might be good to get some sleep.

passages.title: Une amie a besoin de réconfort
passages.french:
— Léa, ça va ? Tu as l'air abattue.
— Pas vraiment... J'ai raté mon entretien ce matin.
— Oh non, je suis vraiment désolée pour toi.
— Je me sens nulle, j'ai attendu ce poste pendant des mois.
— Ne t'en fais pas, ça va aller. Ce n'est qu'une occasion parmi d'autres.
— J'ai peur de ne jamais trouver de travail qui me plaît.
— Je comprends ce que tu ressens, mais tu ne dois pas perdre espoir.
— Merci de m'écouter, ça me fait du bien.
— À ta place, je prendrais un peu de repos avant de recommencer à chercher.
— Tu as raison. Merci d'être là pour moi.
— Toujours ! Tu n'es pas seule, on trouvera une solution ensemble.
— Ça me touche beaucoup. Je me sens déjà plus sereine.
passages.english:
— Léa, are you okay? You look down.
— Not really... I failed my interview this morning.
— Oh no, I'm really sorry for you.
— I feel useless, I'd been waiting for this job for months.
— Don't worry about it, it'll be okay. It's just one opportunity among others.
— I'm scared I'll never find work that I enjoy.
— I understand what you're feeling, but you shouldn't lose hope.
— Thanks for listening, it does me good.
— If I were you, I'd rest a little before starting to search again.
— You're right. Thanks for being here for me.
— Always! You're not alone, we'll find a solution together.
— That really touches me. I already feel calmer.
